translations.text: Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, and so on.
Matthew the Evangelist wrote in the gospel narrative, saying: "The Lord came to a district which is called Caesarea Philippi, and asked his disciples what people said about him.
They answered, 'Some people say that you are John the Baptist, some say that you are Elijah, some Jeremiah, or some other prophet.'
Then the Saviour said, 'Who do you say that I am?' Peter answered him, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'
The Lord said to him in answer, 'Blessed are you, Simon, child of the dove, for flesh and blood did not reveal this faith to you, but my Father who is in heaven.'
I tell you that you are of stone, and upon this stone I will build my church, and the gates of hell can do nothing against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven;
and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."
Bede the commentator reveals to us the depth of this reading, and says that Philip the tetrarch built the city of Caesarea, and in honour of the emperor Tiberius, under whom he ruled,
gave the city the name 'Caesarea', and for his own remembrance added to that name 'Philippi', thus saying 'Caesarea Philippi', as if the city were so named in honour of them both.
When the Saviour drew near to that district, he asked what worldly people said about him.

not as though he did not know what people were saying about him. Rather, he wished to stamp out the false opinion of erring men through the true confession of the right faith. His apostles answered him,
"Some people say that you are John the Baptist, some say that you are Elijah, some Jeremiah, or one of the prophets."
Then the Lord asked, "Who do you say that I am?" as if he had said, 'Now that worldly people know me so erroneously, you who are gods, how do you know me?'
The commentator said 'gods' because the true God, who alone is Almighty, has granted this honour to his chosen ones, so that he calls them gods.
The obedient Peter answered him, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
He said 'of the living God' to distinguish him from the false gods which heathen peoples, deceived by various errors, worshipped.
Some of them believed in dead giants, and set up costly images to them, and said that they were gods because of the great strength that they had;
yet their life was very wicked and shameful. Of this the prophet said,
"The images of the heathen are of gold and of silver, the handiwork of men: they have a dumb mouth and blind eyes, deaf ears and hands that cannot grasp, feet that cannot walk, a body without life."
Some of them believed in the sun, some in the moon, some in fire, and in many other created things; they said that they were gods because of their beauty.
Now Peter clearly distinguished the true faith when he said, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."

He is the living God who has life and being through himself, without beginning, and who created all creatures through his own Son, that is, his Wisdom, and gave life to them all through the Holy Spirit.
In these three persons there is one Godhead, one nature, and one work, undivided.
The Lord said to Peter, "Blessed are you, son of the dove." The Holy Spirit was seen above Christ in the likeness of a dove.
Now the Saviour called Peter "son of the dove," because he was filled with innocence and with the grace of the Holy Spirit. He said,
"Flesh and blood did not reveal this faith to you, but my Father who is in heaven." By "flesh and blood" is meant his fleshly kindred.
He did not have that understanding through human teaching; rather, the Heavenly Father, through the Holy Spirit, gave this faith into Peter's heart.
The Lord said to Peter, "You are of stone." He received that name for the strength of his faith and for the steadfastness of his confession,
because he joined himself with a firm mind to Christ, who is called 'stone' by the apostle Paul.
"And I will build my church upon this rock": that is, upon the faith that you confess.
All God's church is built on that stone, that is, on Christ; for he is the foundation of all the buildings of his own church.
All God's churches are counted as one church, and it is built of chosen people, not of dead stones; and the whole building of those living stones is laid upon Christ;
because through the faith we are counted as his limbs, and he is the head of us all. Whoever does not build from that foundation, his work falls to great ruin.

The Saviour said, "The gates of hell shall have no power against my church." Sins and heretical teaching are the gates of hell, because they lead the sinful man, as if through a gate, into the torment of hell.
Many are those gates, but none of them can prevail against the holy church, which is built upon the firm rock, Christ;
because the believer, through Christ's protection, escapes the perils of devilish temptations.
He said, "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven."
That key is not golden, nor silver, nor forged from any material; rather, it is the authority that Christ gave him, that no one comes into God's kingdom unless Saint Peter opens the entrance for him.
"And whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."
He now gave this power to Peter. Later, before his ascension, he also gave it to all his apostles, when he breathed on them and said,
"Receive the Holy Spirit: the sins of those whom you forgive shall be forgiven; and from those to whom you refuse forgiveness, forgiveness shall be withheld."
The apostles will not bind any righteous person with their excommunication, nor will they mercifully loose the wicked person, unless he turns with true penance to the way of life.
The Almighty has granted the same authority to bishops and holy mass-priests, if they keep it carefully according to the ordinance of the gospel.
But the key is entrusted to Peter in particular so that all nations may clearly recognize
that whoever departs from the unity of the faith that Peter then confessed to Christ will be granted neither forgiveness of sins nor entry into the heavenly kingdom.
After this gospel we will relate to you, in a short account, the way of life and the end of the apostles; for their passion is fully set out in many places in the English language.
After the Lord's ascension Peter preached the faith to the peoples called Galatia, Cappadocia, Bithynia, Asia and Italy.

Afterwards, after a period of about ten years, he went to the city of Rome, preaching the gospel; and in that city he set up his episcopal see, and remained there twenty-five years, teaching the Roman citizens the glories of God, with great miracles.
Throughout all his journeys his adversary was a certain sorcerer, who was called Simon.
This sorcerer was so greatly filled with the accursed spirit that he said that he was Christ, the Son of God, and with his sorcery he corrupted the people's faith.
Then it happened that the body of a widow's son was being carried to the place where Peter was preaching. He then said to the people and to the sorcerer,
"Approach the bier, and believe that the preaching of the one who raises the dead man to life is true." Then Simon was emboldened by the devil's spirit and said,
"As soon as I raise the dead man, kill my adversary Peter." The people answered him, "We will burn him alive."
Then, by the devil's craft, Simon made the dead man's body move. The people then thought that he had been brought back to life.
Then Peter cried out above everyone, "If he has been brought back to life, let him speak to us and stand up; let him taste food and go back home."
Then the people shouted with a loud voice, "If Simon does not do this, he shall suffer the punishment that he intended for you."
Simon was angered by these words and began to flee, but the people seized him with immense scorn.
Then the apostle of God approached the body with outstretched arms and prayed thus:
"You, dear Lord, who sent us to preach your faith, and promised us that through your name we could drive out devils, heal the sick,
and raise the dead, raise this boy now, so that these people may know that there is no God but you alone, with your Father and the Holy Spirit."
After this prayer the dead man arose, knelt down, and said to Peter,
"I saw the Saviour Christ, and at your prayer he sent forth his angels to lead me back to life." Then the people cried out with one voice and said,
"There is one God, whom Peter preaches!" They wanted to burn the sorcerer, but Peter prevented them. He said that the Saviour had taught them the rule that they should repay evil with good.
When Simon had escaped from the people, he tied up a huge mastiff inside the gate where Peter was lodging, so that it would suddenly attack and devour him.
Then Peter came and untied the mastiff with this command:
"Run, and tell Simon that he must no longer deceive with his sorcery God's people, whom He bought with His own blood." And at once the dog rushed at the sorcerer and put him to flight.
Peter called after it, saying, "In God's name I command you not to fix a single tooth in his body."
When the dog was not allowed to harm his body, it tore his clothes piece by piece off his back and drove him along the walls, howling like a wolf, in the sight of the people.
Then he escaped from the dog, and for a long time afterwards, for shame, he was not seen in the city of Rome.
Later, after a time, he found someone who spoke on his behalf to the emperor Nero, and it then happened that the accursed persecutor joined the devil's servant to himself in friendship.
When this had been done, Christ appeared to Peter in a spiritual vision and encouraged him with this exhortation:
"The sorcerer Simon and the cruel Nero are filled with the devil's spirit and are plotting against you; but do not be afraid. I am with you, and I will send my servant Paul to you as a comfort,

who will come into the city of Rome tomorrow. And you two together will fight against the sorcerer in spiritual combat and cast him down into the abyss of hell; and afterwards you two will come together to my kingdom with the victory of martyrdom."
Paul did not suffer when he was brought bound to Rome, but some years later, when he had of his own accord returned there again. This truly happened thus.
On the next day Paul came into the city, and each of them received the other with great joy, and for seven months they preached together within the city the way of life to the people.

Then countless people turned to Christianity through Peter's teaching; and also the emperor's consort Livia and the wife of his chief prefect, Agrippina, became so believing that they shunned the company of their husbands.
Through Paul's preaching the emperor's thegns and household servants believed, and after their baptism they would not return to his household.
Then Simon the sorcerer made a bronze serpent that moved as if it were alive; and he made the images of the heathens laugh and move; and he himself was suddenly seen up in the air.
Moreover, Peter healed the blind, and the lame, and those possessed by devils, and raised the dead, and told the people that they should flee the devil's sorcery, lest they be deceived by his tricks.
Then this was made known to the emperor, and he ordered the sorcerer to be brought to him, and the apostles as well.
Simon changed his appearance before the emperor, so that he suddenly seemed to be a boy, and then a grey-haired man; at times in the form of a woman, and then immediately in the form of a youth.
When Nero saw that, he thought that he was the Son of God.
Peter said that he was God's adversary and condemned for false sorcery, and said that he was truly a devil in human form. Simon said,
"It is not fitting that you, O king, should listen to the words of a lying fisherman. But I will not endure this insult any longer: now I will command my angels to avenge me on this fisherman."
Peter said, "I do not fear your accursed spirits; rather, they will become afraid through faith in my Lord." Nero said,
"Do you not fear the powers of Simon, Peter, who shows his divinity by miracles?" Peter said,
"If he has divinity, then let him say what I am thinking, or what I mean to do." Nero said, "Tell me privately, Peter, what you are thinking."
Then he bent to the emperor's ear and told him to have barley bread brought to him secretly. He blessed the bread, broke it, and wrapped it in his two sleeves, saying,
"Now say, Simon, what I thought, or said, or did."
Then Simon grew angry because he could not uncover Peter's secret. By sorcery he made great dogs come there, and they rushed at Peter.
but Peter showed the blessed bread to the dogs, and they immediately vanished from their sight. Then he said to the emperor,
"Simon threatened me with his angels; now he has sent dogs at me, because he does not have divine angels but doglike ones." Nero said,
"What now, Simon? I think we two are beaten." Simon answered, "O good king, no one knows people's thoughts except God alone."
Peter answered, "Without doubt you lie when you say you are God, since you do not know men's thoughts."
Then Nero turned to Paul and said, "Why do you say nothing? Who trained you?
And what have you taught in your preaching?" Paul answered him, "Sir, what answer should I give to this lost apostate?
If you choose to obey his words, you will ruin your soul and your kingdom as well. But I will answer you about my teaching, which you ask about.
The Saviour who taught Peter in his presence taught me as well, by revelation. And I have filled everything with God's teaching, from Jerusalem until I came to Illyricum.
I taught people to love and honour one another. I taught the rich not to exalt themselves and not to set their hope on false wealth, but on God alone.
I taught people of middle rank to be moderate in their food and clothing. I told the poor to rejoice in their poverty.
I urged fathers to train their children with the discipline of the fear of God. I told children to obey their father and mother in their wholesome counsel.
I taught husbands to keep their marriage vows, because what a husband punishes in an adulterous wife, God avenges on an adulterous husband.
I urged married women to love their husbands deeply and to obey them with fear, as their lords.
I taught masters to be gentle to their servants, because master and servant are brothers before God.
I told servants to serve their masters faithfully, as if they were serving God.
I taught all believers to worship one God, almighty and invisible.

I did not learn this teaching from any earthly man. Christ the Saviour spoke to me from heaven and sent me to preach his teaching to all nations, saying, 'Go throughout this world, and I will be with you;
and whatever you say or do, I will justify it.'" Then the emperor was astonished by these words.
Simon said, "Good king, do you not understand these two men's conspiracy against me? I am Truth, but these men oppose me. Now order a high tower to be built, so that I may climb it;
because my angels will not come to me on earth among sinful people. I will ascend to my father, and I will command my angels to fetch you to my kingdom." Then Nero said,
"I want to see whether you fulfil this promise with deeds." Then he ordered the tower to be put up in great haste on a level field, and commanded all his people to come together to this spectacle.
The sorcerer climbed the tower in front of all the people, stretched out his arms, and began to fly into the air.
Paul said to Peter, "Brother, you were chosen by God before me; it is fitting that you bring down this servant of the devil with your prayers,
and I too will bend my knees in that prayer." Then Peter looked at the flying sorcerer and said,
"I adjure you, accursed spirits, in the name of Christ, to let go of the sorcerer whom you are carrying between you." At once the devils let go of him, and he fell and burst into four pieces.
The four pieces stuck to four stones, which remain as a witness to the apostolic victory to this present day.
Peter's patience allowed the hellish fiends to carry him up through the air for a while, so that in his fall he would come down all the more violently;
And so he who a little before had boastfully wanted to fly with a devilish coat of feathers suddenly lost even the use of his feet.
It was fitting that he should be raised up on high, so that he would fall to the earth in the sight of all the people.
Then Nero ordered Peter and Paul to be held in chains, and had a guard set over the pieces of Simon's corpse, for he thought that Simon might rise from death on the third day.
Peter said, "This Simon will not come back to life before the general resurrection, but he is condemned to eternal torments."
Then Nero, the adversary of God, on the advice of his chief officer Agrippa, ordered Paul to be beheaded and Peter to be hung on a cross.
Then Paul, at the executioner's command, submitted to the edge of the sword, and Peter went up to be hanged on a cross. When he was led to the cross, he said to the executioners,
"I ask you, turn my head downward and stretch my feet up toward heaven. I am not worthy to hang as my Lord did.
He came down from heaven to redeem the world, and so his feet were turned downward.
Now he is calling me to his kingdom, so turn the soles of my feet toward the heavenly way." And the executioners granted him this.
Then the Christian people wanted to kill the emperor, but Peter calmed them with these words:
"My Lord revealed to me a few days ago that I should follow in his footsteps through this suffering. Now, my children, do not hinder my way."
"My feet are now turned toward the heavenly life. Rejoice with me; today I receive the reward for my hardship." Then he prayed to his Lord with these words:
"My Saviour, I entrust to you your sheep, whom you committed to me. They will not be without a shepherd when they have you." And with these words he gave up his spirit.
Peter and Paul went together on this day, victorious, to the heavenly dwelling, in the thirty-sixth year after Christ's passion, and they live with him for eternity.
[In Latin:] Therefore Jerome and certain other authors testify that Peter and Paul were martyred together on one day.
Immediately after their passion, handsome men came who were unknown to all the people. They said they had come from Jerusalem because they wanted to bury the apostles' bodies.
They did so with great reverence, and told the people that they could rejoice greatly, because they were allowed to have such protectors near them.
Know also that this most wicked king Nero will not be allowed to hold the kingdom after the killing of these apostles.
It then happened that all the cruel emperor's people together hated him, so much that they unanimously decided that he should be bound and scourged to death.
When Nero learned of the people's plan, he became afraid for his life and hurried away in flight to the woods.
Then word spread that he wandered so long in the forest, in cold and in hunger, until wolves tore him to pieces.
Then it happened after that, that some Greeks seized the apostles' bodies and wanted to carry them away east with them.
Then suddenly there was a great earthquake, and the Roman people hurried there and rescued the bodies, at the place which is called the Catacombs;
and they kept them there for a year and a half, until the places had been built in which they were afterwards laid, with glory and songs of praise.
It is known throughout all nations that many miracles have happened at the apostles' tombs, by the grace of the Saviour, to whom be glory and praise for ever and ever. Amen.
